stem: A 14-year-old with suspected eosinophilic oesophagitis asks which symptom pattern best fits oesophageal dysfunction rather than a brief immediate allergic reaction. Which option is most consistent with oesophageal dysfunction?

options.text: Isolated petechiae after a viral illness

explanation: Chest pain when eating is the correct symptom pattern. This is because chest pain during eating is a feature of oesophageal dysfunction seen in eosinophilic oesophagitis, rather than a brief immediate allergic reaction.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Correct because chest pain when eating is a listed symptom of oesophageal dysfunction in eosinophilic oesophagitis.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because petechiae suggest a different diagnostic pathway and are not a symptom of oesophageal dysfunction.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because rapid-onset urticaria is more typical of an immediate IgE-mediated allergic reaction.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because profuse diarrhoea suggests gastroenteritis rather than oesophageal dysfunction.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because a positive sensitisation test without symptoms does not indicate symptomatic oesophageal dysfunction.
